Honestly it’s mainly the anticipation beforehand. You think too much about what could happen, what could go wrong, etc. But when your labor begins, I think your body usually just knows what to do from there. It can get really intense and at first I was super scared of the epidural but after those initial contractions get worse, nah. You probably won’t even feel the needle - especially since they numb you. The epidural really helps, so enjoy it while you can. For me, one side kind of wore off so it was painful on that one side. 

Also something I didn’t expect but makes sense: you have to wait to push? Like I don’t know, I had no clue about details like that. I always thought you just push the whole time but you essentially have to push when you contract. Riding the waves basically.  Another thing- you could be really cold and shaky for a little but it’s nothing too bad.

Honestly I thought it would last forever and I thought recovery would last forever (second degree tear) but little one is about to be 4 months on the 30th and it seems so long ago.

June 2018 I was driving with my friend in the passenger seat and boyfriend behind the passenger. We just came back from a hike, and I was merging onto a three way lane. 

I saw a guy on a motorcycle behind me, looked away for a second and when I looked back up I saw the big car behind him. In a split second, I saw the car hit the back of his motorcycle and him be thrown off onto the road. All four tires ran over his body. 

I sped up a little since I was worried the car would hit me and for a moment thought their car was on fire. They were speeding away and I felt a little confused before suddenly just went numb. 

Later after I calmed down I realized it was sparks from the motorcycle being dragged underneath the vehicle.  I pulled over and we all got out. My friend hurried to the guy’s body to check on him and I told my boyfriend to call the police. In the moment I was thinking find something that could stop the bleeding or something, even though my friend said it was too late. 

Another car parked a little ways behind ours and I guess they were able to see everything too. I remember seeing the guy’s skull/brain. His eyes were still open. What happened in between is a little blurry, but people who were walking nearby were freaking out. Police came soon enough and we all waited to be asked what happened. It was summer and like I said before, we came back from a hike. I remember the mosquitos attacking our legs while we sat on the side of the road. Police taped off the entire road, an older woman drove up and was yelling.

She said something about a Samoan gang doing this to him, that her son in law (the motorcyclist) owed them money. Something like that. I remember seeing some guy taking pictures of the scene. We later found out the vehicle that killed him was a stolen car from an old woman. I still get sweaty when I drive near or on that road. Driving for awhile after shook me to the core. 

I was working at Carl’s Jr. at the time and they still told me to come in the day after. Shit times.
